We have simulated two groups, one with mean 10 and the other with mean 12. That is, **the average difference between groups is 2 units**. Both groups have sd = 5.

```{webr-r}
#| autorun: true
a <- rnorm(10000, 10, 5)
b <- rnorm(10000, 12, 5)

plot(density(a), col = "steelblue", main = NA, lwd = 3)
lines(density(b), col = "orangered", lwd = 3)
```

**How does sample size affect the p-value** when testing for differences between both groups?

Choose a **sample size** per group and see the **resulting p-value** from a t-test:

```{webr-r}
#| out.width: '95%'
n <- 3    # sample size per group

a.sample <- sample(a, n)
b.sample <- sample(b, n)

t.test(a.sample, b.sample)
```

Here we show all the resulting p-values with **sampling sizes ranging from 3 to 1000**:

```{webr-r}
#| out.width: '95%'

n <- 3:1000
pvalue <- vector(mode = "numeric", length = 998)
for (i in n) {
  a.sample <- sample(a, i)
  b.sample <- sample(b, i)
  pvalue[i-2] <- t.test(a.sample, b.sample)$p.value
}

plot(n, pvalue)
```
